title: Mitigating OTP Data Leakage Risks in Advanced SoCs Through Secure Storage Architectures
centralThesis: OTP reverse engineering must not become secret reverse engineering.
copilotAnswerRule: Return claim, claimStatus, evidenceLevel, scope, applicability, limitation, sourceUrl, reviewedDate and openQuestion together.

records.title: RP2350 establishes a public physical-access threat case
records.claim: Public RP2350 disclosures document multiple physical paths that bypassed control assumptions or approached recovery of antifuse OTP state.
records.applicability: Threat motivation for SoCs that store usable secrets or security configuration directly in OTP.
records.limitation: The findings apply to the disclosed RP2350 implementation and do not prove identical exploitability for every OTP macro or SoC.
records.openQuestion: Which attack classes and effort levels are in scope for the target OIP implementation?

records.title: FIB/PVC can reveal antifuse physical state
records.claim: IOActive reported extraction of antifuse bit-cell contents from RP2350 using passive voltage contrast with a focused ion beam.
records.applicability: Demonstrates that bit-cell opacity is not a sufficient final confidentiality boundary for valuable secrets.
records.limitation: Equipment, preparation, skill, time, and exact recoverability depend on the device and target data layout.
records.openQuestion: What invasive-readout evaluation has been completed on the target macro and node?

records.title: Secure Storage combines four security functions
records.claim: The disclosed solution integrates antifuse OTP, SRAM PUF, an AES-256 cryptographic engine, and a Secure Controller with address scrambling.
records.applicability: Defines the product architecture and integration boundary presented to advanced-node SoC teams.
records.limitation: Public architecture disclosure does not establish implementation-specific resistance to FI, SCA, or invasive analysis.
records.openQuestion: Which countermeasures and evaluation reports apply to the exact licensed configuration?

records.title: The root key is reconstructed rather than permanently stored
records.claim: The SRAM PUF generates a device-specific root at power-up; the vendor states that this root is never stored on-chip.
records.applicability: Reduces permanent root-secret residency and separates storage readout from root recovery.
records.limitation: Runtime key exposure, helper data, reconstruction logic, scan paths, fault behavior, and zeroization remain assurance targets.
records.openQuestion: What is the measured key-residency window and how is zeroization verified?

records.title: AES-256 creates the confidentiality boundary for OTP contents
records.claim: OTP contents are protected by AES encryption and decryption using 256-bit keys derived from the SRAM-PUF root.
records.applicability: Changes the intended consequence of physical OTP recovery from plaintext retrieval to ciphertext retrieval.
records.limitation: Confidentiality depends on cryptographic implementation, modes, key derivation, integrity policy, FI/SCA resistance, and lifecycle correctness.
records.openQuestion: Which crypto assurance evidence and attack evaluations apply to the delivered engine?

records.title: OTP readout can be decoupled from secret recovery
records.claim: When encryption, scrambling, key reconstruction, controller policy, and lifecycle controls all hold, physical OTP recovery should yield scrambled ciphertext rather than a usable secret.
records.applicability: Central system-security thesis for the OIP presentation.
records.limitation: This is a composed inference, not a certified result; every dependency requires configuration- and node-specific closure.
records.openQuestion: Which evidence demonstrates the composed outcome on target silicon?

records.title: Advanced-node OTP has published silicon evidence
records.claim: Synopsys publicly lists advanced-node OTP as silicon-verified in TSMC N3P, N4P, N5, N5A, N6, N7, and N7A, with N5A and N7A Grade 1 qualification to AEC-Q100.
records.applicability: Supports platform readiness discussion for OIP audiences.
records.limitation: OTP macro availability does not automatically prove Secure Storage release, PUF integration, or security evaluation for every listed node.
records.openQuestion: What exact node and macro are targeted, and which Secure Storage deliverables are released for that configuration?

records.title: Attack resilience remains an evidence gate
records.claim: Architecture documentation alone is insufficient to claim resistance to scoped physical attacks on a specific implementation.
records.applicability: Defines the validation workstream and prevents overclaiming in the OIP deck.
records.limitation: No product-specific FI/SCA/invasive report was supplied for this knowledge package.
records.openQuestion: Who owns the evidence plan, target assurance level, laboratory scope, and acceptance criteria?
